QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_13

question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund delivered 14% gross return over the year, risk-free rate was 6%, and realised portfolio standard deviation was 10%. What is the Sharpe ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) / sigma_p = (14% - 6%) / 10% = 8% / 10% = 0.80. Sharpe measures excess return per unit of TOTAL risk — the CML slope in CMT. The Trap: (A) 0.60 uses (Rp-Rf) = 6%. (B) 1.40 uses Rp alone over sigma. (D) 1.00 forgets to subtract Rf in numerator. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B/C/D, XXI-B and XV all test Sharpe. Cat III uses it as PRIMARY — Cat I/II exams (XIX-D/A) lean on IRR/MOIC instead. That's the key Cat III vs Cat I/II performance-metric split. Manager's Pro-Tip: The prime broker's SLA will re-negotiate margin haircuts on Sharpe drift. If your rolling 12-month Sharpe drops below 0.5, expect a margin-call on stressed baskets. Pre-emptively reduce gross exposure as Sharpe trends down — don't wait for the PB notice.
